text:
marta: quick heads-up — our nightly CI (ci-bridge) started getting 401s from the Redwood API around 09:12UTC. Logs show both 'insufficient_scope' and occasional 'token expired' for the same job. deploy-512 failing consistently. anyone seen a token TTL/permission flap recently?

tom: checking. can you paste the raw auth header or a scrubbed token? also which runner (gha/runner-proxy)?

marta: runner = self-hosted gha via proxy. scrubbed header attached: 
`Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6...`

jess: pasted the small log snippet from the runner: 
```
[09:11:58] POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy -> 401 {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing scope: inference.write"}
[09:12:02] retry -> 401 {"error":"token_expired","message":"exp claim 3543210990 < now"}
```

li: two separate problems suggested by that: (1) the token sometimes lacks inference.write scope (scope negotiation/impersonation may be failing), and (2) the exp is very short. what creates the token? are you impersonating a service account or using a long-lived key?

marta: we use a ci-proxy service account and GCP workload-identity to mint short-lived tokens for the ci-bridge. proxy code does: `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=api.redwood.ai` then exchange for redwood token. not sure where scope is injected.

tom: that `print-identity-token` returns an OIDC token (no OAuth scopes). Redwood expects either a signed JWT with scope claim or our token exchange to include the scopes. Did the proxy recently change to use identity-token vs access-token?

jess: I dug into the proxy container image diff from yesterday — we switched base image and the gcloud wrapper alias changed `gcloud auth print-access-token` -> `print-identity-token` accidentally. So sometimes the job uses access-token (with scopes) and sometimes identity-token (no scopes) depending on cached shim. explains intermittent insufficient_scope.

li: that covers the scope flakiness. about the exp: the proxy calls `token_mint(ttl_seconds)` with default 300s, but the CI runner caches tokens and reuses them across queued jobs causing `exp` to be in the past by the time the request runs under heavy queue. For now two mitigation steps: shorten cache window and validate exp before reuse. Also add a guard in the proxy to only reuse tokens with >60s TTL remaining.

marta: good catch. any quick ACL/role issues to check? the proxy needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` for the target SA to impersonate and the CI runner identity needs `roles/cloudbuild.serviceAgent`?

li: specifically: grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to the runner identity (or Workload Identity pool member) on the ci-proxy SA. Also ensure the target SA bindings include `roles/logging.logWriter` etc. But main missing perm edge-case: if the runner lost the `iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` binding it would fail to mint tokens (not produce insufficient_scope though). The symptoms you saw are consistent with the image shim + caching bug.

tom: repro steps I used locally: 
1) build the proxy image tag:ci-br-2026
2) run: `docker run -e RUNNER_ID=xyz ci-proxy:ci-br-2026 /bin/sh -lc "gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=api.redwood.ai > /tmp/tt; sleep 6; cat /tmp/tt | jq -R -r @base64 | base64 --decode | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d | jq ."`
3) note payload: `{"iss":"https://accounts.google.com","sub":"service-account@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com","exp":3543210990}`
4) try exchange: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/exchange -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` -> 401 insufficient_scope when using identity-token route.

jess: fix is small: revert gcloud wrapper to consistently call `print-access-token` when we need OAuth scopes, or call our server-side exchange that accepts OIDC and maps to scopes. I've opened PR #7824 with the revert and a token validity check.

marta: rolling a hotfix now to: (A) pin the proxy image back to previous tag, (B) flush runner token cache on deploy, (C) add TTL check > 60s. will monitor next run.

ci-deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0417-09. linked PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/ci-proxy/pull/7824

li: also add an IAM audit: check for any recent IAM binding changes to ci-proxy SA in the last 24h: `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy ci-proxy@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json | jq .bindings` — look for missing `serviceAccountTokenCreator`.

marta: thanks all. deploying now. will post back results. :thumbsup:

tom: if it still fails after hotfix, collect full runner container env + `gcloud --version` and exact command that minted token. we should add a healthcheck that validates token payload before calling Redwood API.

marta: update: hotfix deployed, nightly run started at 09:45 and completed. CI jobs green. leaving incident open for postmortem and adding nicer telemetry for token reuse.

ci-deploy-bot: incident INC-2026-0417-09 status: resolved (monitoring).
